findings.summary: SpeedRunner's public project site demonstrates compact presentation/rollout sidecars and codebook snapshots, but the observed sidecars are not replay-admission proofs.
Exact future ASI replay-admission provenance is reducible in current public architecture because WakeSleepLoop already passes a per-batch sleep_trace_path that ASISleep discards.

The observed SpeedRunner main/releases/gh-pages surfaces still do not expose a ScienceWorld Figure-12 numeric run bundle, task-3-only non-replay manifest, environment lock or per-candidate replay transcript.

Current public MemCompiler has two memory time scales: task_memory is fixed after one retrieval within an episode, while the underlying DB can mutate across episodes under current UPDATE_MEMORY=true defaults.

Current MemCompiler detailed trajectories persist memory-count summaries rather than stable candidate identities/digests or pre/post DB snapshots, so they cannot prove cross-condition same-M identity.
MemCompiler's project webpage publishes ScienceWorld results as a plot image but no machine-readable result/run/memory binding; presentation image is not an evaluated-memory-state bundle.
All observed MemCompiler public main commits postdate arXiv v2; current public code cannot be identified as the historical evaluated revision without an explicit provenance bridge.
Current late-code defaults such as UPDATE_MEMORY=true must not be retroattributed to the arXiv-v2 experiment absent a run manifest or equivalent bridge.
MemCompiler backend record IDs exist in Chroma but are erased at the receiver-facing Document-to-MASMessage retrieval boundary.
Equality of receiver-visible returned content is weaker than equality of persistent storage record lineage when equivalent/duplicate records are possible.
Future exact receiver-memory lineage can be captured read-only as backend ID + canonical content digest sidecar without changing the existing model-visible MASMessage values.

Flight Recorder directly implements a claim-authorization split: a ready eval plan and raw aggregate movement are not claim authority; claim authority is downstream of imported evidence and integrity.

Flight Recorder cross-arm comparability is content-bound: matching scenario labels/IDs are insufficient when per-scenario SHA-256 fingerprints differ, and a single source cannot authorize cross-arm claims.

Flight Recorder external-eval claims bind exact held-out manifest, raw per-case result, runner observation/metadata, normalizer contract and complete case coverage; this is protocol corroboration, not scientist-agent causal evidence.

protocol_relation.reason: The new evidence strengthens already-existing evaluation-memory, replay-admission, verifier-observability and evidence-authority boundaries rather than exposing a distinct lifecycle failure class.
